<h>Lectio 1</h>
Léctio sancti Evangélii secúndum Joánnem
<r>Joannes 17:1-11</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Sublevátis Jesus óculis in cælum, dixit: Pater, venit hora, clarífica Fílium tuum. Et réliqua.

Homilía sancti Augustíni Epíscopi
<r>Tractatus 104 in Joannem, sub med.</r>
<c>P</c>óterat Dóminus noster, unigénitus et coætérnus Patri, in forma servi, et ex forma servi, si hoc opus esset, oráre siléntio: sed ita se Patri exhibére vóluit precatórem, ut meminísset nostrum se esse doctórem. Proínde eam, quam fecit oratiónem pro nobis, notam fecit et nobis: quóniam tanti magístri non solum ad ipsos sermocinátio, sed étiam pro ipsis ad Patrem orátio, discipulórum est ædificátio.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Deus, cánticum novum cantábo tibi, allelúia:
* In psaltério decem chordárum psallam tibi, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Deus meus es tu, et confitébor tibi: Deus meus es tu, et exaltábo te.
<r>℟.</r> In psaltério decem chordárum psallam tibi, allelúia, allelúia.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Continuation of the Holy Gospel according to John
<r>John 17:1-11</r>
<c>A</c>t that time, Jesus lifted up His Eyes to heaven, and spoke these words: Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son. And so on.

Homily by St. Augustine, Bishop of Hippo
<r>104th Tract on John</r>
<c>O</c>ur Lord, the Only-begotten and co-eternal Son of the Father, was able, if need were, in and from the form of a servant, to pray in silence, but He thus manifested Himself in prayer, remembering that He is our Teacher. Thus He made known unto us the prayer which He made for us since He was so great a Master that, not only His discourse to them, but His prayer to the Father for them, is an up-building to His disciples. And if it was so for them who were there to hear, truly it is so for us also, for whose instruction it hath been written down.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> I will sing a new song unto thee, O God, alleluia.
* Upon a psaltery of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Thou art my God, and I will praise thee Thou art my God, and I will exalt thee.
<r>℟.</r> Upon a psaltery of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee, alleluia, alleluia.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<c>Q</c>uaprópter hoc quod ait: Pater, venit hora, clarífica Fílium tuum: osténdit, omne tempus, et quid, quando fáceret vel fíeri síneret, ab illo esse dispósitum, qui témpori súbditus non est: quóniam quæ futúra erant per síngula témpora, in Dei sapiéntia causas efficiéntes habent, in qua nulla sunt témpora. Non ergo credátur hæc hora fato urgénte venísse, sed Deo pótius ordinánte. Nec sidérea necéssitas Christi connéxuit passiónem: absit enim ut sídera mori cógerent síderum Conditórem.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Allelúia, audívimus ea in Ephrata, invénimus eam in campis silvæ:
* Introíbimus in tabernáculum ejus, adorávimus in loco, ubi stetérunt pedes ejus, † allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Surge, Dómine, in réquiem tuam, tu et arca sanctificatiónis tuæ.
<r>℟.</r> Introívimus in tabernáculum ejus, adorávimus in loco, ubi stetérunt pedes ejus, † allelúia, allelúia.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<c>W</c>herefore, by these words: “Father, the hour is come, glorify thy Son,” He showeth that all time, and all whatsoever He doth, or alloweth to be done, and the season wherein He will do or allow it, is alike ordained of Him Who is Himself not subject to time. Yea, all things which were then to come, or are yet to come now, have the reason why they should be, in the Wisdom of God, Which is Itself independent of all time. “The hour is come.” We must not believe that that hour was brought on by the march of destiny, but was by ordination of God. No stars decreed irresistibly that the time was come for Christ to suffer God forbid that the revolutions of His planets should force death on Him Who made them.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Alleluia, behold we have heard of it in Ephrata: we have found it in the fields of the wood.
* We will go into his tabernacle: we will adore in the place where his feet stood, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Arise, O Lord, into thy resting place: you and the ark, which you have sanctified.
<r>℟.</r> We will go into his tabernacle: we will adore in the place where his feet stood, alleluia, alleluia.

<h>Lectio 3</h>
<c>C</c>larificátum a Patre Fílium nonnúlli accípiunt in hoc, quod ei non pepércit, sed pro nobis ómnibus trádidit eum. Sed si passióne clarificátus dícitur, quanto magis resurrectióne? Nam in passióne magis ejus humílitas quam cláritas commendátur, Apóstolo teste, qui dicit: Humiliávit semetípsum, factus obédiens usque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Deínde séquitur, et de ejus clarificatióne jam dicit: Propter quod et Deus illum exaltávit, et donávit ei nomen, quod est super omne nomen
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Deduc me in sémita mandatórum tuórum, allelúia, † quóniam ipsam vólui, allelúia
* Inclína cor meum in testimónia tua, † allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Avérte óculos meos ne vídeant vanitátem, in via tua vivífica me.
<r>℟.</r> Inclína cor meum in testimónia tua, † allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Allelúia, allelúia, allelúia.

<h>Reading 3</h>
<c>C</c>ome think that the glorification of the Son by the Father was that “He spared Him not, but delivered Him up for us all.” <n>Rom. viii. 32.</n> But if we say that He was glorified by suffering, how much more shall we say that He was glorified by rising again While He suffered, His humbleness was more manifested than His glory, as witnesseth the Apostle, where he saith “He humbled Himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross” then he addeth touching His glorification “Wherefore God also hath highly exalted Him, and given Him a Name which is above every name, that at the Name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth and that every tongue should confess that our Lord Jesus Christ is in the glory of God the Father.” <n>Phil. ii. 8-11.</n> This is the glorification of our Lord Jesus Christ, that glorification whose first rays dawned on the Resurrection morning.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Make me to go in the path of thy commandments, alleluia, for therein is my desire, alleluia.
* Incline my heart unto thy testimonies, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> O turn away mine eyes lest they behold vanity, and quicken thou me in thy way.
<r>℟.</r> Incline my heart unto thy testimonies, alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> Alleluia, alleluia, alleluia.

b.0856489b62:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>P</c>rídie Nonas Maii Luna tricésima. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>I</h>n Monte Olivéti Ascénsio Dómini nostri Jesu Christi.
<h>R</h>omæ sancti Joánnis, Apóstoli et Evangelístæ, ante Portam Latínam; qui, ab Epheso, jussu Domitiáni, vinctus Romam est perdúctus, et, judicánte Senátu, ante eándem portam in ólei fervéntis dólium missus, exívit inde purior et vegétior quam intrávit.
<h>D</h>amásci natális beáti Joánnis Damascéni, Presbýteri, Confessóris et Ecclésiæ Doctóris, doctrína et sanctitáte célebris. Hic, pro cultu sanctárum Imáginum, verbo et scriptis advérsus Leónem Isáuricum strénue decertávit; cujus Imperatóris ob calúmnias cum ipsi Joánni déxtera manus a Saracenórum Príncipe amputáta esset, idem, beátæ Maríæ Vírgini, cujus Imágines defénderat, se comméndans, prótinus déxteram íntegram sanámque recépit. Ejus autem festívitas sexto Kaléndas Aprílis celebrátur.
<h>C</h>yréne, in Líbya, sancti Lúcii Epíscopi, quem in Actibus Apostolórum sanctus Lucas commémorat.
<h>A</h>ntiochíæ sancti Evódii, qui (ut beátus Ignátius ad Antiochénses scribit), primus ibídem a sancto Petro Apóstolo ordinátus Epíscopus, glorióso martýrio vitam finívit.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Heliodóri et Venústi, cum áliis septuagínta quinque.
<h>I</h>n Cypro sancti Theódoti, Epíscopi Cyríniæ, qui, sub Licínio Imperatóre, gravíssima passus est, ac tandem, in Ecclésiæ pace, spíritum Deo réddidit.
<h>C</h>arrhis, in Mesopotámia, sancti Protógenis, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>I</h>n Anglia sancti Eadbérti, Epíscopi Lindisfarnénsis, doctrína et pietáte insígnis.
<h>R</h>omæ sanctæ Benedíctæ Vírginis.
<h>S</h>alérni Translátio sancti Matthǽi, Apóstoli et Evangelístæ; cujus sacrum corpus, olim ex Æthiópia ad divérsas regiónes et demum ad eam urbem delátum, ibídem, in dedicáta ejus nómine Ecclésia, summo honóre cónditum fuit.

<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.e9c08b5105:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>M</c>ay 6th 2027, the 30th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n Mount Olivet, the Ascension of our Lord Jesus Christ.
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the feast of the holy [Apostle and Evangelist] John before the Latin gate at Rome. He had been brought bound from Ephesus to Rome by command of Domitian, and by the judgment of the Senate he was put into a vessel of boiling oil before the said gate, but he came out thereof cleaner and healthier than he was when he was put therein, [about the year 95.]
<h>U</h>pon the same 6th day of May, were born into the better life:

<h>A</h>t Damascus, [in the year 780,] blessed John of Damascus, famous for holiness and teaching. He strove manfully for the honouring of the holy images, both by word and writing, against the Emperor Leo the Isaurian, wherefore the Emperor commanded that his right hand should be smitten off, whereupon he commended himself to the image of the Blessed Virgin Mary which he had defended, and forthwith he received back his hand whole and sound, of whom we keep feast upon the 27th day of March.
<h>A</h>t Cyrene, [in the first century,] the holy Bishop Lucius, of whom the holy [Evangelist] Luke maketh mention in the Acts of the Apostles, [and the holy Apostle Paul in his Epistle to the Romans.]
<h>A</h>t Antioch, the holy Evodius, who, as the blessed Ignatius writeth unto the Antiochenes, was ordained the first Bishop there, by the holy Apostle Peter, and who finished his life by a glorious testimony, [in the year 62.]
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Heliodorus and Venustus, and seventy-five others.
<h>I</h>n Cyprus, [in the fourth century,] the holy Theodotus, Bishop of Cyrinia, who suffered most grievous persecution under the Emperor Licinius, but saw the peace of the Church before he gave up his spirit to God.
<h>A</h>t Charran, in Mesopotamia, the Bishop Protogenes.
<h>I</h>n England, [in the year 718,] the holy Eadberth, Bishop of Lindisfarne, famous for teaching and godliness, [who held the see of Lindisfarne for eleven years next after holy Cuthbert.]
<h>A</h>t Rome, the holy Virgin Benedicta, [sister of the holy widow Galla.]
<h>A</h>t Salerno, feast is kept for the translation of the holy Apostle Matthew, whose sacred body was brought of old time out of Ethiopia into diverse countries, and at last to that city, where it was buried with all honour under the church dedicated in his name.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, et Spirítui Sancto. Ascéndens.

<r>Hymnus</r>
<c>Æ</c>térne Rex altíssime,
Redémptor et fidélium,
Quo mors solúta déperit,
Datur triúmphum grátiæ.

<h>S</h>candens tribúnal déxteræ
Patris, potéstas ómnium
Colláta Jesu cǽlitus,
Quæ non erat humánitus:

<h>U</h>t trina rerum máchina,
Cæléstium, terréstrium,
Et inferórum cóndita,
Flectat genu jam súbdita.

<h>T</h>remunt vidéntes Angeli
Versam vicem mortálium:
Culpat caro, purgat caro,
Regnat Deus Dei caro.

<h>T</h>u esto nostrum gáudium,
Manens olýmpo prǽditum:
Mundi regis qui fábricam,
Mundána vincens gáudia.

<h>I</h>esu, tibi sit glória,
Qui victor in cælum redis,
Cum Patre, et almo Spíritu,
In sempitérna sǽcula.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Eleváta est, magnificéntia tua, allelúia.
<r>℟.</r> Super cælos, Deus, allelúia.
b.b31326bddd:
<h>Chapter Hymn Verse</h>
<r>Act. 1:1-2</r>
<c>T</c>he former treatise I made, O Theophilus, of all things which Jesus began to do and to teach, Until the day on which, giving commandments by the Holy Ghost to the apostles whom he had chosen, he was taken up.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

Christ ascending.
<r>℣.</r> He led captivity captive. * Alleluia, alleluia.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Ghost. Christ ascending.

<r>Hymn</r>
<c>E</c>ternal Monarch, King most high,
Whose blood hath brought redemption nigh,
By whom the death of death was wrought,
And conquering grace's battle fought:

<h>A</h>scending by the starry road,
This day thou wentest home to God,
By heaven to power unending called,
And by no human hand installed.

<h>T</h>hat so, in nature's triple frame,
Each heavenly and each earthly name,
And things in hell's abyss abhorred,
May bend the knee and own him Lord.

<h>Y</h>ea, angels tremble when they see
How changed is our humanity;
That flesh hath purged what flesh had stained,
And God, the flesh of God, hath reigned.

<h>B</h>e thou our joy, O mighty Lord,
As thou wilt be our great reward;
Earth's joys to thee are nothing worth,
Thou joy and crown of heaven and earth.

<h>A</h>ll glory, Lord, to thee we pay,
Ascending o'er the stars today;
All glory, as is ever meet,
To Father and to Paraclete.
Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Thy magnificence is elevated, alleluia.
<r>℟.</r> Super cælos, Deus, allelúja.
